builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DriftGuard: Online Memory-Drift Detection via Causal Attribution for LLM Agents
summary: DriftGuard replaces online counterfactual replay—re-executing agent trajectories per retrieved memory to detect drift—with an offline stage that builds causal supervision via paired counterfactual replays and trains a lightweight online risk model that scores memories from pre-action information. The cost is a substantial offline data-generation and training pipeline (repeated trajectory replays plus majority-vote aggregation into a memory drift score), while online inference overhead is small; no latency or accuracy figures are given in the abstract. It can fail when the offline counterfactual distribution does not match deployment-time attacks or tasks, when the learned risk model misses drift patterns absent from training, and in settings where the agent has no persistent memory or where building a replay harness over proprietary tool environments is impractical.
rationale: The method targets a real production risk for memory-using agents, but adopting it requires building an offline counterfactual-replay annotation pipeline and training a risk model whose detection quality must be validated on the reader's own agent workload.
technique: Offline causal supervision for online memory-drift detection
